normalized.description: In December 2020, the HSE procured a solution under Emergency Procurement Regulation 32 to support the response to the Covid 19 Immunisation programme. The solution was built on Salesforce CRM platform and provided an immunisation system (Covax) and a public facing support platform (Service Cloud). Due to the extended duration of the pandemic, the ongoing need for comprehensive vaccination management, and a changing patient care pathway, continued integration and expansion of the solution was required to meet Public Health requirements. Covax has undergone significant development over three years, evolving from a MVP into a comprehensive immunisation system capable of managing multiple vaccine types. Covax vaccination platform has evolved to support the following: patient account creation; vaccination recording; full patient vaccination histories; administration of multiple vaccine products; configurable interval times and doses; configurable risk factors; product-based eligibility criteria; adverse reaction capabilities; diverse vaccine administration locations. Additional functionality includes patient portal; appointment scheduling; reporting and analytics; user training platform; support platform; communication platform. With Covax embedded as the core, a network of interconnected software applications, data repositories, integration points, platforms and services have been built up to create the comprehensive and mature national immunisation ecosystem which is in use today. Vaccination records are ingested into Covax from GPs, Pharmacies, and various Community organisations. Data is enriched on Covax through integration with IHI, GP registry, Eircode, and a vaccination asset management system. National vaccination reporting is enabled though integration with the HSE’s data lake. Covax is an established and embedded cornerstone of the national IT infrastructure. It is currently the largest patient database in the HSE, with over 4.4 million patient records and over 16 million recorded vaccinations. The architecture of the Covax system is proven in terms of both performance and scale, with the recording of 400,000 vaccinations per week at peak. The Covax public-facing portal has facilitated the self-registration of 2.2 million patients for vaccination to date and appointment scheduling functionality has created over 7.5 million appointments. Since 2021, Covax has ingested over 6 million vaccination records from GPs and 2 million from pharmacies. To date, over 20,000 clinical and operational staff have been trained to use the Covax system. Embedded in the pandemic response was the requirement for HSE Live to provide public-facing support. Salesforce Service Cloud was used to provide this support, and with extensive and incremental development, this generic platform was tailored for use by multiple Covid support teams across the HSE including HSE Live, DCC team, HSE NSD (National Service Desk), Covax support and GP Resolver teams.

Title: Germany – Spacecraft, satellites and launch vehicles – QYRO PETER FM Platform
Procedure title: QYRO PETER FM Platform
Description: The QYRO project is a joint effort of Robert Bosch GmbH, Q.ANT, Trumpf Photonic Components, Trumpf Laser Berlin, Ferdinand-Braun-Institut, Leibniz-Institut für Höchstfrequenztechnik (FBH), and the German Aerospace Center Galileo Competence Center (DLR-GK). Its purpose is to promote Germany’s role in the space sector by demonstrating the performance of a miniaturised next generation quantum optical gyroscope and therefore pave the way for a commercial use of this new technology for a German company on the promising New Space market. Therefore, the project shall design and develop a miniaturized, high precision nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) Gyroscope for the use in the satellites. This quantum-based gyro – QYRO – shall be launched and validated in space against state-of-the-art attitude determination systems for CubeSat missions. For that purpose, DLR’s task in this project is to establish the definition and design of the mission to host the QYRO unit. Followed by supporting the other project partners to manufacture a space qualified version of the ground based QYRO unit. Additionally, DLR KN with the support from GK, will integrate GALANT phased array antenna for space positioning applications, which additionally will be investigated in a first approximation to make the interference detection function usable in space. The payload will be constituted by two QYRO units, the GALANT electronics module together with its antenna module, a reference gyroscope and finally a payload computer. The mission will be launched into an SSO with an apoapsis and periapsis height under 600 km. In terms of operations, communications and the payload on-board computer software, the valuable experience of DLR-SC and DLR-RB will contribute to a successful operation of the CubeSat. The last stage of the project would comprise launching and operating the CubeSat in space to conduct the in-orbit validation test campaign. The Contractor shall be responsible of providing the 16U platform for the Flight Model of PETER, support its integration and testing, contribute to the tools for its control and, additionally, providing the payload computer together with the necessary libraries and tools required to implement the payload control software on it. Further details about the Contractor requirements and responsibilities have been defined in the attached Specification of Services.

Its purpose is to promote Germany’s role in the space sector by demonstrating the performance of a miniaturised next generation quantum optical gyroscope and therefore pave the way for a commercial use of this new technology for a German company on the promising New Space market. Therefore, the project shall design and develop a miniaturized, high precision nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) Gyroscope for the use in the satellites. This quantum-based gyro – QYRO – shall be launched and validated in space against state-of-the-art attitude determination systems for CubeSat missions. For that purpose, DLR’s task in this project is to establish the definition and design of the mission to host the QYRO unit. Followed by supporting the other project partners to manufacture a space qualified version of the ground based QYRO unit. Additionally, DLR KN with the support from GK, will integrate GALANT phased array antenna for space positioning applications, which additionally will be investigated in a first approximation to make the interference detection function usable in space. The payload will be constituted by two QYRO units, the GALANT electronics module together with its antenna module, a reference gyroscope and finally a payload computer. The mission will be launched into an SSO with an apoapsis and periapsis height under 600 km. In terms of operations, communications and the payload on-board computer software, the valuable experience of DLR-SC and DLR-RB will contribute to a successful operation of the CubeSat. The last stage of the project would comprise launching and operating the CubeSat in space to conduct the in-orbit validation test campaign. The Contractor shall be responsible of providing the 16U platform for the Flight Model of PETER, support its integration and testing, contribute to the tools for its control and, additionally, providing the payload computer together with the necessary libraries and tools required to implement the payload control software on it.
